title: Why metal feels colder than wood at the same temperature
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why does metal feel colder than wood?
Are metal and wood the same temperature?
Why do tiles feel cold on bare feet?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: Same temperature, different speed of heat flow

explain.say: Touch a metal bench and a wooden one on the same morning and the metal feels much colder. Yet if you measured them, both would be at the same temperature as the air.

draw.text: Why metal feels colder than wood at the same temperature

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Same temperature, different speed of heat flow

explain.say: Your hand is warmer than both. Metal is a good conductor, so it pulls heat out of your skin quickly and carries it away. Your skin cools down, and you feel cold.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Same temperature, different speed of heat flow

explain.say: Wood is a poor conductor. It takes heat from your hand only slowly, so the skin you touch it with stays warm, and the wood feels warmer.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Same temperature, different speed of heat flow

explain.say: Your skin does not sense temperature directly; it senses how fast it loses or gains heat. That is also why metal in hot sunshine feels hotter than wood: it pours heat into you fast.

faq.q: Are metal and wood really the same temperature?
faq.a: Yes. Left in the same room, everything settles to the room's temperature. A thermometer would read the same on both; only the feel is different.

faq.q: Why does a metal bench feel cold?
faq.a: Metal conducts heat very well, so it draws heat out of your warm skin quickly. Losing heat that fast is what your skin reports as cold.
asks: Why is metal cold to touch?

faq.q: What do our skin nerves actually sense?
faq.a: They mostly sense the temperature of your own skin and how fast it is changing. So a material that draws heat away fast feels colder than one that does not.
asks: How does skin feel hot and cold?

faq.q: Why does metal feel hotter on a hot day?
faq.a: When metal is hotter than your skin, it pours heat into you quickly for the same reason, so it feels hotter than wood at the same temperature.
asks: Why do metal slides burn in summer?

faq.q: Why do tiles feel colder than carpet?
faq.a: Tile and stone conduct heat much better than carpet, which is full of trapped air. Your bare feet lose heat faster on tiles, so they feel cold.
asks: Why is a stone floor cold on bare feet?

facts: Your skin senses how fast it is losing or gaining heat, not the true temperature of what you touch.
Steel conducts heat roughly 100 to 400 times better than wood.
